subject.title: [Feature Request] Hook Chain Integrity Protection Against Message Tampering

question: What hook-chain security model should OpenClaw support for mutable plugin hooks: host-owned audit/provenance only for today’s in-process plugins, integrity checks across a future isolated-plugin IPC boundary, or a per-hook permission system first?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but implementing checksums, audit logs, or per-hook allowlists would encode a security boundary and plugin compatibility policy that current source and docs do not settle.

options.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
options.body: Document the threat model, redaction/retention rules, and compatibility plan before implementation touches hook runner behavior or config.

options.title: Ship redacted audit first
options.body: Add host-owned audit events for modifying hooks while deferring checksum enforcement and per-hook allowlists.

options.title: Defer behind sandbox work
options.body: Keep this blocked on the broader process-isolation/security-profile items so integrity checks are designed only for an IPC boundary.

recommendation.title: Define audit and trust boundary first
recommendation.body: Document the threat model, redaction/retention rules, and compatibility plan before implementation touches hook runner behavior or config.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has repeated recent history on hook runner, hook contract, and hook docs surfaces that would carry this design into implementation.
